text:
Florida is missing its heart. Aleksander Barkov (knee) is out until late November and Brad Marchand (knee) until around Nov. 21, and the Panthers are 2-3-0 in their last five. The new arrival has been the bright spot: Brady Tkachuk, now playing alongside his brother Matthew, has a four-game point streak and six points in four games against Columbus. Their father Keith has been in the headlines too, quoted by theScore saying "It's time Ottawa moves on."

Our numbers say Florida is better than its record. The Panthers have a +1 goal difference on +6.9 expected and 53% of the expected goals, which means finishing has cost them about six goals. Jacob Markstrom has not helped either, at .886. Florida also takes 5.8 penalties a game, which is a lot even for a team that draws nearly as many.

Columbus has a goalie on a run. Cam Talbot is .940 with 8.6 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Kent Johnson has a seven-game point streak with 11 points, and Zach Werenski has six games in a row with a point. The Blue Jackets lost Conor Garland indefinitely, per Daily Faceoff, and come off a 5-2 loss in Buffalo, but they have had three days of rest to Florida's one. At five on five they've taken 49% of the expected goals.

Our numbers lean Florida, 3.36 to 3.08. Sam Reinhart (41% to score, seven points in four games against Columbus) and Matthew Tkachuk (74% for a point) lead the way. Our sleeper is Adam Fantilli, 52% for a point, above his season pace. Mathieu Olivier is one goal from 50 for his career.
headline: Panthers are hurt; Talbot is hot

hunch.text: Florida's chances say it should win; our gut says a rested team with the hotter goalie and no Barkov to solve doesn't care. Columbus takes it.
